summary: 14-day analysis of Nightscout telemetry shows strong overall Time in Range (86.0%) with an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL. However, Time Below Range (5.1%) exceeds safety guidelines, concentrated in early night (01:00 local TBR 18.5%) and late afternoon (19:00 local TBR 15.3%). Zero carbohydrates were logged across the period, forcing 100% reliance on unannounced meal detection (UAM) and Dynamic ISF. This creates postprandial glucose spikes followed by delayed automated insulin stacking and subsequent hypoglycemia. Safety limits (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) are exceptionally wide relative to daily insulin needs (~19.7 U/day).

analysis_steps.findings: Continuous CGM coverage is 98.7% over 14 days with minor gaps. Telemetry contains 655 insulin delivery events and 6,214 device status entries. Zero carbohydrate entries were logged in Nightscout treatments, creating a major data gap for meal absorption analysis.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries across 14.0 days; total_carbs_g = 0.0g; insulin_entries = 655.
data_gaps: Lack of carb logging prevents direct calculation of true Carb Ratio (CR) efficacy and precise meal absorption curves.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall glycemic control is high (86.0% TIR), but hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR) exceeds the 4.0% safe threshold. Bimodal hypo peaks occur overnight at 01:00 local (18.5% TBR) and late afternoon at 19:00 local (15.3% TBR).
analysis_steps.evidence: Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL): 86.0%; Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL): 5.1%; hourly peak lows at 01:00 local (18.5% TBR) and 19:00 local (15.3% TBR).
data_gaps: Unannounced meals obscure whether afternoon lows are driven by basal excess or accumulated SMB microboluses.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight fasting between 04:00 and 08:00 local is stable (95.2-98.7% TIR), indicating baseline basal rates (0.6-0.7 U/h) are appropriate during fasting. Nocturnal hypos between 23:00 and 03:00 are driven by post-dinner UAM SMB accumulation paired with a low overnight target of 90 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Fasting BG 04:00-08:00 averages 99.5-106.0 mg/dL; Target set to 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00; 01:00 TBR 18.5%.
data_gaps: Requires isolating post-dinner IOB decay from baseline basal stability using logged meal events.

analysis_steps.findings: Base profile ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U with DIA at 10.0 hours. Dynamic ISF reduces correction factor down to 27-38 mg/dL/U during postprandial surges, driving heavy automated insulin delivery that over-corrects 3-4 hours later.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile ISF = 56 mg/dL/U; DIA = 10h; variable_sens dynamic ISF logs reach 27.8 mg/dL/U during high excursions.
data_gaps: True static ISF vs Dynamic ISF compensation cannot be separated without announced meal boluses.

analysis_steps.findings: System relies entirely on uam_enabled=true and smb_always_enabled=true with a 3-minute delivery interval. When unannounced meal spikes occur, microboluses stack rapidly, delivering excessive insulin late in the absorption curve.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_interval_minutes = 3; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes = 20; UAM boost logs show microbolusing up to 1.6 U during glucose surges.
data_gaps: Absence of carb announcements forces loop to react defensively after glucose has already risen.

analysis_steps.findings: Max Basal (12 U/h) and Max IOB (25 U) are excessively high for a patient using ~19.7 U total daily insulin. These limits provide minimal protection against over-dosing during sensor noise or unannounced meal spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour = 12.0 U/h; max_iob_units = 25.0 U; total daily insulin average = 19.71 U/day.

analysis_steps.findings: All meals are currently unannounced. Postprandial glucose peaks between 10:00 and 16:00 local (TAR reaching 32.1% at 16:00) trigger reactive UAM SMBs, causing late postprandial drops into hypo at 18:00-19:00 local.
analysis_steps.evidence: 0g carbs logged; hourly_glucose_local peak average 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local followed by 15.3% TBR at 19:00 local.
data_gaps: Lack of user-logged prebolus or meal timing data prevents measuring exact postprandial recovery curves.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbohydrate entries are used. Slowly absorbed meals managed strictly by UAM lead to prolonged late-stage microbolusing, directly contributing to nocturnal hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_treatment_entries = []; zero extended carbs; high nocturnal TBR (18.5% at 01:00 local).
data_gaps: Specific meal composition (fat/protein content) is unrecorded.

analysis_steps.findings: System instability is primarily caused by unannounced meals interacting with aggressive Dynamic ISF and loose AAPS safety limits, aggravated by an overnight target of 90 mg/dL. Primary intervention must focus on safety limit reduction and overnight target elevation before adjusting CR/ISF parameters.
analysis_steps.evidence: Total daily insulin ~19.7 U vs Max IOB 25 U; 01:00 TBR 18.5%; Fasting BG 04:00-08:00 is stable at ~100 mg/dL.
data_gaps: Validation requires 3-5 days of consistent carbohydrate logging alongside tightened safety limits.

strengths: High CGM sensor data coverage (98.7%) over 14 days with negligible data gaps.
Excellent fasting baseline stability from 04:00 to 08:00 local (average glucose 99.5-106.0 mg/dL, TIR >95%), proving basal rates are well-tuned during un-influenced fasting.
Strong overall Time in Range (86.0%) demonstrating effective automated algorithm recovery despite challenging unannounced meal dynamics.
issues: Hypoglycemia exceeds recommended safety thresholds (5.1% TBR vs <4.0% clinical target), peaking at 01:00 local (18.5% TBR) and 19:00 local (15.3% TBR).
Safety limits are set excessively wide (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) relative to average total daily insulin requirement (~19.7 U/day).
Zero carbohydrates are logged in Nightscout, forcing total reliance on reactive UAM microboluses and dynamic ISF scaling down to ~28 mg/dL/U.
Overnight glucose target (90 mg/dL) provides an insufficient buffer against post-dinner IOB decay and CGM noise.

recommendations.title: Lower Max IOB and Max Basal Ceilings in AAPS
recommendations.description: Current safety ceilings (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) are disproportionately high compared to daily requirements (~19.7 U/day total), creating unnecessary risk during unannounced meal surges or sensor errors. Reduce Max IOB to 7.0 U (~35% of TDD) and Max Basal to 3.5 U/h.

recommendations.title: Elevate Overnight Target Segment to 100 mg/dL
recommendations.description: Nighttime glucose drops into hypoglycemia frequently (01:00 local TBR 18.5%). Raising overnight target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL (23:00 to 08:00) adds a necessary safety buffer while carb logging is established.

recommendations.title: Introduce Meal Carb Announcements with Preboluses
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrates were logged over 14 days, forcing 100% reliance on reactive UAM SMBs and Dynamic ISF. Prebolusing or logging meal carbs 10-15 minutes prior will prevent late postprandial insulin stacking and late afternoon hypos.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Increase overnight glucose target segments (23:00 to 08:00) from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Recurrent early-night hypoglycemia (up to 18.5% TBR at 01:00 local) indicates that a 90 mg/dL overnight target leaves zero margin for error against post-dinner IOB decay and CGM variance. Baseline fasting glucose from 04:00-08:00 is stable at ~100 mg/dL, confirming 100 mg/dL is a realistic and safe target.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for 3-5 days to confirm TBR from 23:00-04:00 drops below 4.0%.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery frequency is appropriate provided Max IOB safety limit is capped.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max IOB (25 U) and Max Basal (12 U/h) are dangerously high for a patient taking ~19.7 U total daily insulin. Reducing Max IOB to 7.0 U (~35% TDD) and Max Basal to 3.5 U/h caps runaway automated delivery during unannounced meal surges or sensor noise.
Dynamic ISF (70%) provides necessary responsiveness for unannounced meals; capping Max IOB will safely restrain its over-correction risk.
Standard min_5m_carbimpact (8 mg/dL/5min) and 7h max absorption are appropriate for oref1 algorithm.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition from complete reliance on unannounced meals (UAM) to upfront carb logging with a 10-15 minute prebolus. If exact carb counting is difficult, log estimated partial carbs or use short e-carbs (2-3 hour duration) to give the loop early visibility and prevent late SMB stacking.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Zero carbs logged over 14 days causes the loop to react late to meal spikes via UAM and Dynamic ISF. This delays peak insulin delivery, resulting in afternoon peaks (16:00 TAR 32.1%) followed by late postprandial hypoglycemia (19:00 TBR 15.3%).
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal carbs and bolus timing for 3-5 consecutive days to evaluate if prebolusing reduces both the 2-hour postprandial spike and 4-hour post-meal drop.

exceptions.pattern: High-fat or high-protein late evening meals
exceptions.suggestion: Use e-carbs (3-5 hour extended duration) rather than relying solely on UAM or a single upfront bolus.
exceptions.rationale: Slow meal absorption without e-carbs triggers prolonged UAM microbolusing late into the night, driving nocturnal hypoglycemia (01:00 TBR 18.5%).

implementation_steps: Discuss safety ceiling changes with the healthcare team before updating AAPS settings.
Reduce AAPS Max IOB to 7.0 U and Max Basal to 3.5 U/h in AAPS preferences to establish protective dosing caps.
Update the profile target segments from 23:00 to 08:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL to reduce nocturnal hypoglycemia risk.
Begin logging meal carbohydrates in Nightscout/AAPS with a 10-minute prebolus for routine meals.
Monitor CGM telemetry for 5-7 days after changes, verifying that Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) drops below 4.0% before considering any further profile adjustments.
education: Unannounced meal detection (UAM) reacts to rising glucose rather than preventing it. Because insulin action takes 15-30 minutes to peak, reactive microboluses often stack late in the digestion cycle, causing a drop 3-4 hours after eating.
Max IOB safety limits should ideally reflect a safe fraction of total daily insulin (typically 30-40% of TDD). Setting Max IOB higher than total daily insulin eliminates algorithm safety guardrails.
A flat target of 90 mg/dL overnight leaves narrow tolerance for sensor noise or small amounts of lingering insulin on board (IOB) after dinner.
safety_notes: This decision-support analysis is for informational review only and does not constitute medical advice or prescriptions.
All proposed parameter changes must be independently reviewed and approved by a qualified healthcare professional.
Make adjustments one parameter at a time, allowing at least 3 to 5 days of monitoring between changes.
Prioritize safety limit corrections (Max IOB) and hypoglycemia prevention before attempting to tighten glycemic targets or adjust carb ratios.
